newsitem.title: UK: UK Liberal leader warns of public debt crisis.
newsitem.headline: UK Liberal leader warns of public debt crisis.

text.p: Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown said on Tuesday that Britain could face a public borrowing crisis after the next election following the doubling of the national debt in the past six years.
But he added that despite his calls for some increases in income tax, he had no intention of returning "to the punitive taxes of the last Labour government."

In his keynote speech to his party's pre-election annual conference, Ashdown confirmed that the party wanted to raise income tax for those earning over 100,000 stg a year to 50 percent from the present 40 percent.
And he said he was willing to raise the standard rate of tax by a penny in the pound if the money was needed to fulfil a pledge to raise annual education spending by two billion stg.
"But we can guarantee this. We will never let Britain return to the punitive taxes of the last Labour government," he said.
Ashdown said the doubling of Britain's national debt meant that servicing it was now costing the equivalent of seven pence in the pound on income tax.

"This country now faces a real problem-- perhaps even a crisis -- with public borrowing after the next election," he said. "That is the real tax bombshell in Britain -- the one that both of them (Labour and the Conservatives) are trying to hide," he said.
